title: Forest Fire Ash Optimizer (FFA): A Novel Physics-based Metaheuristic Algorithm for Implementing Exploration-Exploitation Flexible Regulation
abstract: Abstract This study proposes a novel physics-inspired metaheuristic algorithm named Forest Fire Ash Optimizer (FFA). Inspired by the characteristics of ash movement in different forest fire burning stages, intelligently transformed these regular behaviors into a variety of unique algorithmic mechanisms, including a four-population mechanism based on fitness and denseness partitioning, an inverse proportionality selection mechanism for elite influence, and an ash movement strategy grounded in actual physical phenomena. These components complement each other to enable flexible regulation of exploration and exploitation, i.e., the two phases are not merely sequential, but change dynamically depending on the search status of FFA agents. To verify the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm, FFA is qualitatively analyzed using the CEC-2022 test suite. Additionally, the classical standard test suite, CEC-2017 test suite, and CEC-2022 test suite are conducted to compare the performance of FFA with 9 advanced algorithms. The results demonstrate that FFA excels in performance, exhibiting high stability, flexibility, and robustness. Finally, FFA is applied to 9 classical and challenging real-world engineering optimization problems. The results indicate that, compared to the competing algorithms, FFA provides superior and more novel solutions, predicting its potential for in-depth applications in more engineering fields.
